answer_to_user: Valuing banks on price-to-book (the right multiple for banks, not P/E): out of a 367-bank US+European universe, 73 trade below 1x book. Sorted by ROE so you can separate cheap-and-sound from cheap-and-impaired — the P/B and ROE must be read together. Best combinations (well below book AND solidly profitable): Nova Ljubljanska Banka (NLB.LSE) at 0.23x book with 12.4% ROE, Thurgauer Kantonalbank (TKBP.SW) 0.37x / 9.4%, Deutsche Bank (DBK.XETRA) 0.78x / 9.2%, Credit Agricole (ACA.PA) 0.78x / 9.1%, Societe Generale (GLE.PA) 0.82x / 8.9%, Barclays (BARC.LSE) 0.88x / 9.9%, Bank OZK (OZK.US) 0.88x / 11.0%, and BNP Paribas (BNP.PA) 0.91x / 10.5%. Among US regionals, OptimumBank (OPHC.US) and Citizens Holding (CIZN.US) sit just under book with the highest ROEs (~13-14%). Rule of thumb from this list: a bank near 1x book with double-digit ROE is arguably fairly-valued; the ones to scrutinise for a "broken bank" are any deep-discount names whose ROE is low — a big discount to book with weak ROE is the classic cheap-for-a-reason trap. (I required ROE>0 so genuinely loss-making banks are already excluded.)
